passage:
Monday. After his tantrum, Rishi sobbed. Tanuja started a lecture. He cried harder.
Wednesday. Rishi's crying turned to sobs. He held out his arms. Tanuja hugged him and gave him water. Zeenat didi breathed slowly beside them. Rishi's body got soft.
Friday. Rishi sobbed, then leaned into Tanuja on his own. She held him. He sipped water and sighed.

qa.q: What did Tanuja give Rishi on Wednesday?
qa.a: She gave him water after hugging him.

qa.q: What did Rishi want when he held out his arms?
qa.a: He wanted comfort and a hug, as his big feelings were settling.

qa.q: What did Tanuja learn between Monday and Wednesday?
qa.a: She learned that a lecture made it worse, while a hug, water and slow breathing helped Rishi settle.

qa.q: How might Zeenat didi see Rishi's change by Friday?
qa.a: She may notice he now leans in on his own, trusting that comfort will come.

grounding: It shows a toddler whose crying turns to sobs and who reaches out or leans in, needing a hug, water and slow breathing rather than a lecture.

passage: In their Bengaluru flat, Golu had been crying on the floor for a long time. Now the crying turned to small sobs. He lifted his arms toward Manjula. She picked him up and held him close. "Shh, shh." Devika Masi brought a small cup of water. Golu sipped, then leaned his head on Manjula's shoulder. She breathed slowly, and his breaths slowed too.

qa.q: Who brought Golu a cup of water?
qa.a: Devika Masi brought him a small cup of water.

qa.q: What did Golu want when he lifted his arms?
qa.a: He needed comfort, wanting to be held after his big cry.

qa.q: What helped Golu's body settle?
qa.a: Being held close, a sip of water and Manjula's slow breathing helped him calm down, without any lecture.

qa.q: How might Manjula feel holding Golu?
qa.a: She may feel relieved and tender as his breathing slows. 😊

grounding: It illustrates a toddler whose crying becomes sobs, who reaches out to be held and settles with a hug, water and slow breaths.

passage:
Monday. Madhav screamed on the floor after his bath and pushed Sonali's hands away. She waited nearby.

Wednesday. Another storm, over socks. When the screams became sobs, he crawled closer to Sonali.

Saturday. After crying over a broken biscuit, Madhav reached out both arms, sobbing. Sonali held him, gave him water and breathed slowly. His breathing slowed with hers.

qa.q: What upset Madhav on Saturday?
qa.a: A broken biscuit.

qa.q: How can you tell Madhav feels ready for comfort on Saturday?
qa.a: He reaches out both arms while sobbing, showing he feels sad and wants to be held.

qa.q: What helped Madhav's body settle?
qa.a: A hug, a sip of water and slow breathing with Sonali, rather than any lecture.

qa.q: How might Sonali feel when Madhav reaches out?
qa.a: She probably feels relieved and tender, glad he now comes to her for comfort.

grounding: Over a week toddler Madhav's storms end with sobs and reaching out, and a hug, water and slow breathing help his body settle.

passage:
In their Chennai flat, little Anand had screamed for ten minutes over a popped balloon. His father, Lalit, sat close by.

Slowly the screams became hiccuping sobs. Anand looked up, face wet, and held out his arms.

Lalit didn't say, "See, I told you it would pop." He just picked Anand up and held him close.

He gave him water and breathed slowly, his chest rising against Anand's cheek.

Anand leaned in. His sobs grew quieter, and his fingers curled into Lalit's shirt.

qa.q: Why had Anand been screaming?
qa.a: Because his balloon had popped.

qa.q: What does Anand holding out his arms show?
qa.a: It shows he feels sad and tired after the storm and now wants comfort.

qa.q: What did Lalit do that helped Anand's body settle?
qa.a: He hugged him, gave him water and breathed slowly, without any lecture about the balloon.

qa.q: How might Lalit feel as Anand curls his fingers into his shirt?
qa.a: He probably feels relieved and tender, glad the storm is passing.

grounding: As toddler Anand's crying turns to sobs he reaches out, and his father's hug, water and slow breathing help his body settle, with no lecture.

passage:
"Papa... Papa..."

"I'm here, Madhav."

"Ball... gone..."

"The ball went over the wall. I know."

"Up. Up."

"Come here. Up you come."

"Sad..."

"You're sad. Here, sip some water."

"...Water."

"Good. Let's breathe. In... and out."

"In..."

"And out."

"...Out."

"That's it. Papa's got you."

Madhav rested his wet cheek on Dhruv's shoulder. His sobs slowed down, one by one.

qa.q: Where did the ball go?
qa.a: Over the wall.

qa.q: What does Madhav saying "Up. Up." show about what he needs?
qa.a: It shows he feels sad and wants comfort and to be held, not a lecture.

qa.q: What helped Madhav settle?
qa.a: Being picked up, a sip of water, and slow breathing with Dhruv.

qa.q: How might Dhruv feel holding Madhav?
qa.a: He is probably calm and caring, relieved that Madhav is coming down from the storm.

grounding: In dialogue toddler Madhav, winding down from tears, reaches to be held, and a hug, water and slow breaths from his father help him settle.

passage: Note for Sudha, from the daycare room, Tuesday. Sumit had a big cry at pick-up time today when the blocks were packed away. After a few minutes the screaming turned into hiccupping sobs. Then he held out both arms to me. I picked him up, no lecture, and just held him. I gave him a sip of water and breathed slowly with him until his chest settled. He rested his head on my shoulder. He was calm and smiling by the time you came.

qa.q: What set off Sumit's big cry?
qa.a: The blocks were packed away at pick-up time.

qa.q: What did Sumit's outstretched arms suggest he needed?
qa.a: He was winding down and needed comfort, feeling tired and sad but ready to be held.

qa.q: Why did the note-writer skip the lecture?
qa.a: At this stage Sumit needed comfort rather than words: a hug, a sip of water and slow breathing helped his body settle.

qa.q: How might Sudha feel reading this note?
qa.a: Sudha would probably feel reassured and grateful that Sumit was comforted and calm by pick-up.

grounding: Shows a toddler's crying easing into sobs as he reaches out, and a caregiver offering a hug, water and slow breaths instead of a lecture.
